pl-l4d26c6-d1e115.summary: Holds that since marriage is a sacrament, it is a sacred sign and of a sacred thing, the union of Christ and the Church, as Paul says of 'two in one flesh': this is a great sacrament, in Christ and the Church. As spouses are joined by consent of minds and mingling of bodies, so the Church is joined to Christ by will and nature, willing what he wills and he taking the form of human nature: spiritually and bodily, by charity and conformity of nature.
claims: Marriage signifies the union of Christ and the Church.
That union is by charity and by nature.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e124.summary: States that marriage figures both unions: the spouses' consent signifies the spiritual union of Christ and the Church by charity; the mingling of sexes the union by conformity of nature.
claims: Consent signifies union by charity; carnal union signifies union by nature.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e127.summary: Notes that hence some doctors said a woman who does not experience carnal union does not belong to marriage.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e131.summary: Quotes Augustine: there is no doubt that a woman with whom there was no mingling of sexes does not belong to marriage.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e140.summary: Quotes Leo: since the society of marriage was so instituted that without the mingling of sexes it does not contain the sacrament of Christ and the Church, a woman in whom the nuptial mystery did not occur does not belong to marriage.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e146.summary: Adds Augustine: there is no perfect marriage without mingling of sexes.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e155.summary: Warns that taken literally these would lead one to say marriage cannot be contracted without carnal union, and that between Mary and Joseph there was no marriage, or no perfect one; which is wicked to think, since it was holier and more perfect the freer it was from carnal work.
claims: Mary and Joseph's marriage was true and perfect.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e158.summary: Interprets these texts: not that a woman without carnal union does not belong to marriage, but that she does not belong to the marriage that bears the express and full figure of Christ's union with the Church. It figures the union in charity but not the union in conformity of nature by which members are joined to the head through the assumption of flesh. Such marriage is no less holy, since, as Augustine says, in marriage the holiness of the sacrament counts more than fertility.
claims: Unconsummated marriage figures only the union of charity.

pl-l4d26c6-d1e167.summary: Adds that marriage is also a sign of the spiritual union and love of minds by which spouses should be united, as Paul says: husbands, love your wives as your own bodies.
claims: Marriage signifies the spouses' union of love.

pl-l4d26c6.summary: As a sacrament, marriage is a sacred sign of a sacred thing, the union of Christ and the Church: as spouses are united by consent of minds and mingling of bodies, the Church is joined to Christ by will and nature, by charity and conformity of nature. Some doctors say a woman without carnal union does not belong to marriage, but taken literally this would deny that Mary and Joseph were truly or perfectly married, which is wicked; their marriage was holier the freer from carnal work. These texts mean such a marriage does not fully figure Christ's union with the Church, only the union of charity, not of nature; yet it is no less holy. Marriage also signifies the spiritual union of love between spouses.
claims: Marriage signifies the union of Christ and the Church.
Consent signifies union by charity; carnal union signifies union by nature.
Marriage without carnal union is true marriage, as with Mary and Joseph.
Such marriage figures only the union of charity, yet is no less holy.
Marriage signifies the spouses' union of love.
